title: LandlordGuard Customer Relief on the RentGuard Reinstatement Fee
content:
A customer reinstating a RentGuard Renters Policy who also insures a rental building under the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy receives relief on the reinstatement fee according to how long that LandlordGuard policy has been held.

## Guidance

- When the customer holds a LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy in force whose original effective date is 36 or more whole months before today, 3.00 is taken off the fee.
- When that LandlordGuard policy's original effective date is 12 or more but fewer than 36 whole months before today, 1.50 is taken off.
- When the customer holds no LandlordGuard policy in force, or one held fewer than 12 whole months, no relief applies.

## Points of judgement

- **In force.** Only a LandlordGuard policy whose status is in force counts; a cancelled or expired LandlordGuard policy gives no relief.
- **Length of holding.** Counted in whole months from the original effective date shown on the LandlordGuard policy to today.

| LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy | Whole months since its original effective date | Taken off the fee |
|---|---|---|
| in force | 36 or more | 3.00 |
| in force | 12 to 35 | 1.50 |
| in force | fewer than 12 | nothing |
| none in force | not applicable | nothing |

**Boundaries.** 11 whole months: nothing; 12 whole months: 1.50; 35 whole months: 1.50; 36 whole months: 3.00.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A hypothetical customer whose LandlordGuard policy has been in force since 40 whole months ago has 3.00 taken off the reinstatement fee; one whose LandlordGuard policy started 5 whole months ago has no relief.
